references.text: Earlier mention of the same priestly garments made of blue, purple, and scarlet wool for service in the sanctuary
God's command to make the priestly garments and the holy vestments for the priest Aaron
The original instructions for Aaron's holy garments, including the use of blue, purple, and scarlet wool
Description of the ephod to be made from gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet wool, and finely twisted linen
Summary of the priestly garments for service in the sanctuary and the holy vestments for the priest Aaron
Use of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric in connection with sanctuary service
Reference to the fact that priests serve in a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of the heavenly one, as Moses was commanded
Specifies that the belt, as part of the holy garments, is made with the same colored threads and under the same divine command mentioned in the source verse.
Provides the original specification for which garments were to be made, giving context to the execution described in the source verse.
Specifies the making of the tunics as a concrete part of the general production of woven garments mentioned in the source verse.
Follows the natural narrative sequence: first the making of the garments (Exodus), then the dressing during consecration (Leviticus).
